newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ CURVE FLATTENS AS SHORT END RECOVERS WITH NZD.
newsitem.headline: NZ CURVE FLATTENS AS SHORT END RECOVERS WITH NZD.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous trading day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (SEP) 91.83 (PREV 91.74) 90-DAYS 8.42 (PREV 8.52) 3-YR BONDS (SEP) 92.65 (PREV 92.70) 02/01 7.28 (PREV 7.28)
OVERNIGHT CASH 8.30 PCT (PREV 8.25) US 5-YR 6.26 (PREV 6.20) NZD/USD 0.6421/28 (PREV 0.6391/98) US 10-YR 6.42 (PREV 6.37)
New Zealand's yield curve flattened on Wednesday as bank bill yields fell on a firming currency and bond yields rose with U.S. treasuries.
Dealers said the currency was looking quite perky as the Australian dollar recovered and the bill market would continue to remain bid as long as the currency held.
At 5.10 p.m. (0510 GMT) the kiwi was at US0.6421/28 from its 0.6395/02 opening.
A chief forex dealer said 0.6425 was a critical level.
"If we close above it tonight I think there is a chance we will push higher. I think the aussie has probably turned around and it looks like that might go higher overnight as well.
"There is a chance for both to strengthen a little more," he said, adding that the kiwi had formed a base around 0.6410 with initial resistance at 0.6450-55.
Bond dealers said the local market will hinge on U.S. treasuries action which will depend on U.S. PPI and retail sales data due tonight.
There is concern that inflation was starting to feed through to the U.S. economy and the last 20 points of the selloff of local bonds had all been related to the U.S. market.
The domestic market appears to be getting comfortable with the Monetary Conditions Index nearly 100 basis points easier than the Reserve Bank's desired level.
"It's a watering down effect. That's why the short end has been able to perform okay today," one chief dealer said.

Another dealer commented that although conditions had technically eased significantly, most of that had come via the currrency and that did not appear to be an inflationary pressure in a weak economy.
The dealer said there was aggressive buying in the bill futures by the same bank that pushed the kiwi up from 0.6410.
The September bill futures closed at 91.83 on volume of 2739.
The physical bills are in a 8.50-20 percent range with good selling interest around 8.20 percent.
The Food Price Index rose 0.8 percent in July, higher than forecasts, and that was a slight negative for the market.
